subject: Post-call: CascadeHealth compute reservation path — isolation, burst scaling & SLA
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Cole <hannah.cole@cascadehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 07 May 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: CascadeHealth compute reservation path — isolation, burst scaling & SLA

Hi Hannah — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Key pain points you described:
- Production triage model needs low p95 latency (~100ms) for 512-token requests (inference path).
- Heavy burst traffic around morning clinic syncs (short windows with 3–4x baseline QPS).
- PHI / HIPAA constraints: model inference must run in an isolated environment with customer-managed KMS and audit logs retained for 12 months.
- Current procurement window: ~6–8 weeks to sign and onboard.

Goals we heard:
- Dedicated, isolated pool to avoid noisy neighbors and simplify audits.
- Ability to sustain baseline 200 req/sec and absorb 800 req/sec bursts with <150ms median and p95 <=100ms.
- SLA target: 99.9% availability for inference endpoints; tighter p95 latency SLOs during business hours.

What we propose (next steps / ask list):
1) Technical workshop with your infra + ML infra folks (we recommend Evelyn to lead infra runbook discussion).
2) Share initial sizing spreadsheet (attached) — please fill in expected concurrency and token distributions; we’ll convert to A100-equivalent GPU counts.
3) Draft MOP / SOW for a 3-month POC reserved pool + canary rollout plan (attached draft MOP).
4) Security checklist: we’ll attach SOC2 summary and a short FAQ on KMS / VPC options. If you want, we can pull a short audit package for procurement.

Proposed timeline:
- This week: you confirm workshop attendees and procurement contact.
- Next week: technical workshop (60–90 min).
- Following 2 weeks: sizing finalization and draft SOW for procurement.

Attachments: [Attachment: cascade_sizing_spreadsheet.xlsx (xlsx)] [Attachment: redwood_dedicated_mop_draft.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks — I’m looping in Ben (SE) and Evelyn (infra) to coordinate the workshop.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-call: CascadeHealth compute reservation path — isolation, burst scaling & SLA

Thanks Kimberly — this looks accurate and helpful. Couple clarifications from our side:

- The 512-token request is our longest common case; median is closer to 128 tokens but peaks hit 512.
- For bursts: we need fast vertical scaling for short windows rather than long-term overprovisioning. Can Redwood support burst capacity that taps reserved pool + short-term burst credits?
- Procurement: procurement@cascadehealth.com will require SOC2 doc and an export-control question set (I’ll send our vendor security form).
- SLA: 99.9% is fine to start; we may negotiate p95 latency SLOs in the SOW if the numbers are there.

We can do the technical workshop next Tue 10–11am PT. Attendees: me (ML), Diego (platform engineer), and Megan (security).

I’ve attached a short vendor security questionnaire for you to review — it’s small, hope that’s okay.

—Hannah

Subject: Re: Post-call: CascadeHealth compute reservation path — isolation, burst scaling & SLA

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Hannah. Short answers to your asks:

- Burst capacity: yes — we can provision a reserved baseline pool and add a configurable burst bucket that uses spare capacity in the cluster (policy-driven). We’ll include clear cost/latency tradeoffs in the sizing sheet.
- Proposed starter footprint for the POC (ballpark): 8 A100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool with autoscale to +50% for bursts, plus a small hot-cache tier for short-lived KV states. That should comfortably hit your baseline and the morning burst windows without long-tail queuing.
- Security materials: Kimberly — we’ll attach SOC2 summary and redact any sensitive ops notes; Evelyn can confirm retention and KMS flow for PHI.

Next steps I’ll take on:
- Update the sizing spreadsheet with the A100-equivalent estimate and burst policy rows.
- Draft a mutual action plan and push the MOP/SOW into your Drive link.
- Schedule the tech workshop for Tue 10–11am PT.

Ben
